name: Coastal and Marine System Science, Ph.D.
department: Department of Physical and Environmental Sciences

deadline.value: Fall priority deadline for full admissions and funding consideration is January 10, 2027; international final deadline for Fall is June 1, 2027 (domestic final deadline July 17, 2027).
deadline.quote: International Students: | Final deadline for receipt of complete applications: | Fall - June 1 | *Priority deadline to receive complete applications: | Fall - January 10 | *Complete application should be received for full admissions and funding consideration

gre_general.value: The program admissions webpage states GRE scores are waived until further notice (though the 2026-2027 catalog text still prints general test scores).
gre_general.quote: GRE scores waived until further notice

toefl_min.value: Program requires a higher TOEFL minimum than the university baseline: 79-80 iBT (or 550 paper-based).
toefl_min.quote: Official TOEFL score minimum paper-based score of 550 or internet-based score of 79-80

ielts_min.value: Program requires a minimum IELTS Academic score of 6.5 (higher than the 6.0 university baseline).

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists in Environmental or Earth Sciences; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics, and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Applicants must contact program faculty, identify a willing graduate supervisor before applying, include a summary of those discussions in their essay, and will not be admitted without a supervisor.
supervisor.quote: Persons seeking admission to the program should first contact the program faculty and identify a faculty member, or members, willing to serve as the graduate supervisor, and the applicant must include a summary of their discussions with faculty members in their essay. Applicants will not be admitted to the program without a graduate supervisor.

funding.value: Teaching assistantships, graduate research assistantships, scholarships, and competitive NSF CREST-GEIMS Doctoral Fellowships ($1,800-$2,400/month plus tuition and fees) are available; Marine Biology and CMSS Ph.D. programs jointly award at least 20 assistantships yearly, and 50% FTE appointments waive non-resident tuition under Texas Education Code 54.212.
funding.quote: Teaching Assistantships, graduate research assistantships, fellowships, or scholarships may be available to graduate students admitted as degree-seeking students

also.quote: Each year, the Marine Biology and Coastal and Marine System Science PhD programs award at least 20 graduate assistantships to students.

The NSF CREST-GEIMS Center at TAMU-CC offers a competitive Fellowship to Ph.D. students pursuing doctoral degrees in Coastal and Marine Systems Science (CMSS) or Computer Science with a Geospatial focus at TAMU-CC.

According to the Texas Education Code, Section 54.212, non-resident students receiving a 50% FTE graduate assistantship will receive in-state tuition and fees at the rate charged to Texas residents for the semester in which they hold the assistantship appointment.

entry_route.value: Applicants may enter with either a bachelor's degree (90 SCH minimum) or a master's degree (60 SCH minimum).
entry_route.quote: Each student accepted to the CMSS Ph.D. degree program must complete a minimum of 90 hours beyond the bachelor’s degree or 60 hours beyond the master’s degree

notes: Interdisciplinary Earth System Science Ph.D. integrating biogeochemistry, geospatial information science, ecosystem dynamics, and quantitative modeling. The 2026-2027 catalog still prints GRE required and an older Dec 1 Fall deadline, whereas the current CMSS program webpage specifies GRE waived until further notice and January 10 priority / June 1 international final Fall deadlines.
